chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about what is obligatory upon a man regarding the charity of fiṭrah for his household.
He said: “Give charity on behalf of everyone whom you maintain, whether free or enslaved, young or old, among those who have reached the prayer.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the Eid prayer, marking the relevant time for fiṭrah liability
key_terms.تَصَدَّقْ: give charity; here, pay the fiṭrah due
key_terms.حُرٍّ: a free person under one’s care
key_terms.صَدَقَةِ الْفِطْرَةِ: the obligatory charity of fiṭrah given at the end of Ramaḍān
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: an enslaved person under one’s care

ai.seo_question: For whom must a man pay Ṣadaqat al-Fiṭrah in his household?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling of Ṣadaqat al-Fiṭrah for a man’s dependents. It indicates that fiṭrah is to be given on behalf of all those under his maintenance, including free persons, slaves, children, and adults, provided they are present at the time of the prayer.
